title: Building standards for Mendix
about: What MxScout finds wrong in a Mendix model, turned into how to build it right. Every security check MxScout runs (public/secrisks.js, and the mendix-describe skill's check-security.js, which runs the same file) has one entry here, under the check's own id: the risks it reports carry that id in theirs ('mx-' + the check's id + '-' + what it is about). Each entry says what is wrong, the standard to build by, how to fix a model that already has it, Mendix's own code where Mendix has one, and where it comes from. Two more parts hold standards no check of MxScout's reaches: what an agent judges by the risk levels (risk-levels.md), and Mendix's naming conventions. Edit standards.json; standards.md is made from it by tools/build-standards.js, and the test suite fails when a check has no entry here.
use: Refining a story that changes the model: name the standards it touches by id (for example 'anon', 'scope-write', 'conv-microflow-prefix'), and build to them. Fixing a risk MxScout reported: the part of its id after 'mx-' and before the subject is the entry to read.

checks.name: Security level
checks.wrong: Security is Off or Prototype / demo: with Off the running app enforces no rule at all, with Prototype / demo it does not check entity access.
checks.standard: Build with the security level set to Production from the first sprint: every entity has access rules, every page, microflow and nanoflow names the module roles allowed to use it, and Studio Pro's consistency check shows no security errors.
checks.fix: In App Security set Security level to Production, then work through the consistency errors Studio Pro lists: access rules on each entity, allowed module roles on each page, microflow and nanoflow.

checks.name: Demo user password
checks.wrong: A demo user's password is weak: shorter than the project's password policy, a common password, or the same as the user name.
checks.standard: Use demo users only to try the user roles out in development, give each a password that meets the project's password policy, and switch demo users off before the app reaches an environment other people use.
checks.fix: In App Security, Demo users, give the user a strong password or switch demo users off. Switching them off does not remove their accounts from the database: delete those in every environment where they were created.

checks.name: User role without module roles
checks.wrong: A user role carries no module role: somebody given it can sign in and reach nothing.
checks.standard: A user role is a job; it combines at least one module role, and each module role says what that job may do in one module.
checks.fix: In App Security, User roles, add the module roles the job needs, or delete the user role if nobody is meant to hold it.

checks.name: Strict mode
checks.wrong: Strict mode is off: the browser can do more than the app's own pages and flows do when an access rule is set up too wide.
checks.standard: Build with strict mode on in App Security (React client), as a second line behind the access rules, never instead of them; design pages so they fetch only what they define.
checks.fix: Switch strict mode on in App Security, after checking that the pages fetch only what they define.

checks.name: Page URL check
checks.wrong: Strict page URL checking is off: the security of a page reachable only by its URL is not checked by Studio Pro.
checks.standard: Keep Strict page URL checking on in App Security, so Studio Pro's consistency check also checks the pages that are reachable only through their page URL.
checks.fix: Switch Strict page URL checking on in App Security and work through the consistency errors it adds.

mendix.title: App Security: Strict Page URL Checking

checks.name: User role that manages every role
checks.wrong: A user role can assign every other user role, including roles above its own.
checks.standard: Give User management only to the user roles that administer accounts, and name the user roles each may manage instead of all of them; no role manages a role with more rights than its own.
checks.fix: In App Security, User roles, open the role's User management and select only the user roles it is meant to hand out.

checks.name: Published service with nothing in front of it
checks.wrong: A published REST, OData or web service has no list of allowed module roles and no authentication.
checks.standard: Every published REST, OData and web service has authentication and names the module roles allowed to call it; a service meant for anyone is published for the anonymous role on purpose, and gives it only what it publishes.
checks.fix: In the published service's Security settings choose the authentication it needs and select the allowed module roles.

checks.name: Anonymous role (Mendix MXS003–MXS010)
checks.wrong: Anonymous visitors, who never sign in, get more than a visitor needs: sensitive entities, write access, user management, the administrator's role or Administration's module roles, or every row of an entity.
checks.standard: Allow anonymous users only when the app has content for people who do not sign in. Give them a user role of their own (Mendix names it Anonymous), with module roles made for anonymous use alone, read access constrained by XPath, no write on persistable entities and no user management; take a visitor's input in a non-persistable entity and check it in a microflow before anything is stored.
checks.fix: Work through the codes below in App Security and on the access rules of the entities named; if the app has no use for anonymous users, set Allow anonymous users to No.

codes.title: Disable anonymous users
codes.standard: Allow anonymous users = No, unless the app is meant to be used without signing in.

codes.title: Avoid granting anonymous users access to sensitive entities
codes.standard: No access rule for an anonymous module role on an entity that inherits from System (System.User, System.FileDocument and their specializations).

codes.title: Do not use the administrator user role for anonymous access
codes.standard: The anonymous user role is never the administrator's user role.

codes.title: Avoid granting anonymous users write access to persistable entities
codes.standard: No create, write or delete for an anonymous module role on a persistable entity.

codes.title: Do not let anonymous users manage user roles
codes.standard: The anonymous user role has nothing under User management.

codes.title: Do not share module roles between anonymous and other user roles
codes.standard: A module role the anonymous user role carries belongs to no other user role.

codes.title: Do not map Administration module roles to the anonymous user role
codes.standard: The anonymous user role carries no module role of the Administration module.

codes.title: Constrain the read access of anonymous users
codes.standard: Every read rule for an anonymous module role has an XPath that limits the rows to what a visitor may see.

checks.name: Self-registration
checks.wrong: A way to register without signing in (a microflow the anonymous role may run, or a REST operation with no authentication) creates an account with a user role that is administrative, manages other roles, or reads account or personal data without an XPath.
checks.standard: A self-registration flow gives a newcomer one fixed user role, named in the flow, with the least the newcomer needs; never a role taken from the request or decided by a constant, and the role reads personal and account data only through an XPath to [%CurrentUser%].
checks.fix: Give the role the registration flow hands out only what a newcomer needs, and keep personal and account data behind an XPath to [%CurrentUser%].

checks.name: User accounts
checks.wrong: A user role changes other people's accounts, hands out user roles without User management, changes other people's names or e-mail, or reads other people's personal fields.
checks.standard: Account data (System.User and its specializations, such as Administration.Account: name, e-mail, password, active, blocked, user roles) is changed only through User management in App Security, or by a role whose access rule keeps it to its own account with an XPath to [%CurrentUser%]; other people's personal fields are readable only by the roles that need them.
checks.fix: Take write access on the account's fields off the access rule for that role, or constrain the rule with an XPath to [%CurrentUser%]; give account administration to a role with User management of only the roles it may hand out.

checks.name: Hidden on the page, not checked in the flow
checks.wrong: A page hides or disables a button by a condition (the object's state, its owner), and the microflow behind the button does not check that condition: anyone allowed to run the microflow can call it directly.
checks.standard: Every microflow a role may call checks, with a decision at its start, the same condition its page uses to hide, disable or make read-only the button that runs it; what a page shows is convenience, the microflow and the access rules are the security.
checks.fix: Add a decision at the start of the microflow that checks the same condition the page uses to hide the button, and end the flow when it does not hold.

mendix.title: Implementing Best Practices for App Security

checks.name: Microflow retrieves past the role’s XPath
checks.wrong: A microflow that does not apply entity access retrieves objects the role's own access rule keeps from it, and returns them to that role.
checks.standard: A microflow a role may call either applies entity access, or gives every Retrieve the XPath of the role's own access rule; it never hands the client objects its role could not retrieve itself.
checks.fix: Give the Retrieve in the microflow the XPath of the role's own access rule, or let the microflow apply entity access.

checks.name: Two objects of the same entity from the client
checks.wrong: A microflow takes two objects of the same entity from the client and changes one of them, without checking that they belong together.
checks.standard: When a microflow takes more than one object from the client, it checks that they belong together (the same owner, or one associated to the other) before it changes either.
checks.fix: Check in the microflow that the two objects belong together, the same owner or one associated to the other, before it changes either.

checks.name: Written wider than edited
checks.wrong: An access rule lets a role change an attribute in every state of the object, while every page and microflow that role uses edits it only in some states.
checks.standard: When an object may be edited only in some states (a Status enumeration, a Submitted boolean), the role gets two access rules: one that reads every state, and one with the write rights whose XPath names the editable states, such as [Status = 'Draft']. Or the write right is left off and a microflow makes the change after checking the state.
checks.fix: Move the write rights into an access rule whose XPath names the states the pages edit in, or take the write right off and let a microflow that checks the state make the change.

checks.name: Deleted wider than the Delete buttons
checks.wrong: An access rule lets a role delete an object in every state, while every Delete button and microflow the role uses deletes it only in some.
checks.standard: Allow delete only in an access rule whose XPath names the states a Delete button or microflow exists for, or leave delete off and let a microflow that checks the state delete the object.
checks.fix: Move Allow delete into an access rule whose XPath names the states the Delete buttons work in, or take it off and delete through a microflow that checks the state.

checks.name: Write scope
checks.wrong: Worth knowing: one before-commit microflow guards several entities, or a role holds create rights nothing it reaches uses.
checks.standard: Grant create only to the module roles whose pages or microflows create the object; a before-commit event that refuses a change counts as a guard only when it checks the same state the pages do.
checks.fix: Take the create right off the rules where nothing the role reaches creates; check that the shared before-commit microflow refuses what the pages do not allow, or name the state in the access rule.

checks.name: Reads every row, sees fewer
checks.wrong: A read access rule has no XPath, while nothing the role reaches lists every row: a page is not a security boundary, the rule is what the client may fetch.
checks.standard: Every read access rule carries the XPath its pages narrow by, such as [System.owner = '[%CurrentUser%]'] or a path to the current user's account; a rule with no XPath is a decision that every row may be read.
checks.fix: Give each read rule the XPath its pages narrow by, or confirm that every row may be read.

checks.name: Granted, never used
checks.wrong: A module role holds an access rule on an entity that nothing the role reaches shows, reads, takes or returns.
checks.standard: Give a module role an access rule only on the entities its pages, microflows, nanoflows and published services use.
checks.fix: Take the rule off the module role, unless a Java action or a published service needs it.

checks.name: May write, nothing writes
checks.wrong: A module role may write, create or delete an entity, and no input on its pages, no New or Delete button and no flow that runs with its rights does.
checks.standard: Give write, create and delete only where a page, a button or a flow the role runs uses them; read-only is the default.
checks.fix: Take the unused write, create and delete rights off the rule.

checks.name: May run it, may not do what it does
checks.wrong: A microflow or nanoflow a role may run changes, creates or deletes an entity the role has no right on, so it fails for that role.
checks.standard: What a role may run, it can complete: a nanoflow, and a microflow that applies entity access, need the role's rights on everything they change; a microflow that must do more than the role may runs without entity access and checks the caller itself.
checks.fix: Give the roles that may run the flow the access it needs, or stop offering it to them.

checks.name: May run it, finds nothing
checks.wrong: A flow a role may run reads an entity that role cannot read, so it finds nothing for that role.
checks.standard: The module roles allowed to run a flow can read what the flow retrieves, or the flow is not offered to them.
checks.fix: Give the role read access, or stop offering the flow to it.

checks.name: Does for a role what its rules do not allow
checks.wrong: Worth knowing: a microflow does for a role what the role's own access rules do not allow.
checks.standard: A microflow that does for a role what its access rules do not allow is the one controlled way to do it: it checks who calls it and the object's state, and its documentation says why it runs past the rules.
checks.fix: Nothing, if each is the controlled way to let the role do it; otherwise give it the decisions that check the caller and the state.

checks.name: Access rule MxScout cannot follow
checks.wrong: An access rule's XPath goes through the System module and keeps going: MxScout cannot follow it, so the rule is said to be not checked, not to be wrong.
checks.standard: Keep access rule XPaths readable: to the current user through [%CurrentUser%] or System.owner, and otherwise through associations of the app's own modules, not through System members and beyond.
checks.fix: Nothing is wrong by this alone: check the rule in the running app as each role, or rewrite the path through an association of the app's own.

checks.name: Constant the browser receives that looks like a secret
checks.wrong: A constant with Expose to client on has a name or a default value that looks like a key, a password or a token: every browser of the app receives its value.
checks.standard: A secret (an API key, a password, a token, a client secret) is never in a constant with Expose to client, and never a default value in the model: it is in a constant that is not exposed, with no default, set per environment, and read only in microflows.
checks.fix: Switch Expose to client off and empty the default value; set the value in each environment. If the value ever was in the model or reached a browser, replace the secret at its issuer.

checks.name: Constants
checks.wrong: Worth knowing: a constant the browser receives has a default value kept in the model, or a name that is itself a key.
checks.standard: A constant's default value is what a developer runs with locally, never a value of a real environment; each environment sets its own, and a constant's name says what it is, never holds a value.
checks.fix: Empty the default value and set it per environment; rename a constant whose name is a key, and replace that key at its issuer.

checks.name: Known security advisory
checks.wrong: Worth knowing: the Mendix version or a Marketplace module is in the range a published security advisory names.
checks.standard: Keep the Mendix version on a supported patch release and every Marketplace module at a version past each advisory that names it; read the security advisories when upgrading or adding a module.
checks.fix: Upgrade the Mendix version or the module to the version the advisory names as fixed.

checks.name: Administrative role of a Marketplace module on a user role
checks.wrong: A user role that is not the application’s administrator carries the administrative module role of a Marketplace module, so everybody given it may configure the module, run its imports or manage its data.
checks.standard: Give a Marketplace module’s administrative module role only to the administrator’s user role, or to a user role made for the few people who run that module; an ordinary user role carries only the module roles it needs.
checks.fix: In App Security, User roles, take the module role off that user role, and give it to the administrator or to a dedicated user role.

checks.name: Marketplace module the app does not use
checks.wrong: Worth knowing: a Marketplace module is installed and nothing of the app’s own calls its flows, shows its pages or uses its entities.
checks.standard: Install only the Marketplace modules the app uses, and remove a module once nothing uses it any more; a module that stays is kept at a supported version.
checks.fix: Delete the module in App Explorer after checking that nothing outside the model needs it; deleting a module deletes its data.

mendix.title: Implement Best Practices for App Security

checks.name: Marketplace module role that grants nothing
checks.wrong: Worth knowing: user roles carry a module role of a Marketplace module that no access rule, flow, page or published service of the module names.
checks.standard: A user role carries only the module roles that give it something it needs.
checks.fix: In App Security, take the module role off those user roles, unless a newer version of the module needs it.

judged.name: A secret written into the model
judged.standard: No password, token or API key is a constant's default value or a literal in an expression; secrets are set per environment.

judged.name: Delete or bulk change with no check
judged.standard: A microflow that deletes or changes many objects checks who may do it and what the objects belong to before it starts, and deletes only what it was meant for.

judged.name: Service call with no error handler
judged.standard: Every call to a REST, OData or web service has a custom error handler that logs the error and ends the flow in a known way, telling the user when one waits; no call is left to fail silently.

judged.name: Commit inside a loop
judged.standard: Inside a loop, change objects and add them to a list; commit the list once, after the loop.

judged.name: Validated on the page only
judged.standard: What a page validates is validated again in the microflow that saves the object, in a VAL_ sub-microflow both can use.

judged.name: Depends on a switched-off scheduled event
judged.standard: A process that depends on a scheduled event says so in the event's documentation, and whether the event runs is set and checked per environment.

judged.name: Values written into flows
judged.standard: A value that differs per environment or is a business rule (a URL, a limit, a rate) is a constant or a configuration entity, not a literal in a flow.

judged.name: Unused or duplicated
judged.standard: Flows and pages nothing reaches are deleted, not kept as _New, _Old or copies; disabled activities are removed from a flow before it is committed.

conventions.name: Modules and module roles
conventions.standard: A module is named in UpperCamelCase after its responsibility (CustomerManagement, SharePointIntegration) and works as a replaceable service; module roles are named in English after the access they give (Administrator, Employee).

conventions.name: Entities and attributes
conventions.standard: An entity is named in the singular, in PascalCase, without abbreviations or underscores (Customer, LogEntry); attributes in PascalCase (FirstName); an attribute kept only for technical reasons starts with an underscore (_Imported).

conventions.name: Associations
conventions.standard: Keep the association name Studio Pro generates (Order_Customer); when two entities have more than one association, extend each name with its purpose (Person_Address_Delivery).

conventions.name: Folders
conventions.standard: Documents are grouped in folders by process and its steps, and by entity for what belongs to one entity (its overview pages, validation and event microflows); folder names are unique and say what is in them.

conventions.name: Microflow names and prefixes
conventions.standard: A microflow is named {PREFIX}_{Entity}_{Operation} (ACT_Vendor_StartWorkflow): ACT_ for a button or menu item, SUB_ for a sub-microflow, DS_ for a data source, VAL_ for validation, OCH_ / OEN_ / OLE_ for on change, enter and leave, BCO_ / ACO_ / BCR_ / ACR_ / BDE_ / ADE_ / BRO_ / ARO_ for entity events, CAL_ for a calculated attribute, SCE_ for a scheduled event, ASU_ / BSD_ / HCH_ for what after startup, before shutdown and the health check call, CWS_ / CRS_ / PWS_ / PRS_ / POS_ for integrations, WFA_ / WFS_ / WFC_ for workflows, TEST_ or UT_ for unit tests; a microflow that fits none has no prefix.

conventions.name: Page names
conventions.standard: A page ends in its purpose: _Overview, _New, _Edit, _NewEdit, _View, _Select, _MultiSelect, _Tooltip, _Workflow; home pages are Home_Desktop_Default or Home_Desktop_{User role} (and _Tablet_, _Phone_).

conventions.name: Other documents
conventions.standard: Enumerations start with ENUM_ (ENUM_ShippingStatus), snippets with SNIP_, layouts with their device (Responsive_, Phone_, Popup_ …), and integration documents with IMM_, EXM_, XSD_ and JSON_.
